title: What Happens When You Walk Into a Room and Forget Why?
sources: University of Notre Dame, 'Walking through doorways causes forgetting, new research shows' (Gabriel Radvansky, Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology, Nov 2011; college students; virtual rooms: subjects carried an object from table to table and forgot more after passing through a doorway than after covering the same distance in one room; real rooms with objects hidden in boxes gave the same result; returning to the original room did not improve memory; a doorway acts as an 'event boundary' that 'separates episodes of activity and files them away'): https://provost.nd.edu/news/walking-through-doorways-causes-forgetting-new-research-shows

BPS Research Digest, 'How walking through a doorway increases forgetting' (study 1 virtual environment had 55 rooms; participants picked up an object at one table and set it down at the next; memory probed right after an open doorway or halfway across a large room; going back through two doorways to the original room gave no better performance than the second room): https://www.bps.org.uk/research-digest/how-walking-through-doorway-increases-forgetting

Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011), 'Walking through doorways causes forgetting: Further explorations', Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 64(8), 1632-1645, doi:10.1080/17470218.2011.571267

Tease (next video): NHS, 'Why we should sit less' (many adults spend more than 7 hours a day sitting; the Department of Health and Social Care calls inactivity a 'silent killer'; sedentary behaviour is linked to heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and obesity): https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/exercise-guidelines/why-sitting-too-much-is-bad-for-us/

lines.text: What happens when you walk into a room and forget why?
lines.caps: WHAT *HAPPENS | WHEN YOU *WALK | INTO A *ROOM | AND *FORGET WHY?

lines.text: Scientists built fifty-five virtual rooms to test it. Does going back help? Yes or no?
lines.caps: SCIENTISTS *BUILT | *55 ROOMS | TO *TEST IT | GOING *BACK | *HELP? | *YES OR NO?

lines.text: People carried objects through a doorway, or the same distance in one room.
lines.caps: PEOPLE *CARRIED | *OBJECTS | THROUGH A *DOORWAY | OR THE *SAME DISTANCE | IN *ONE ROOM

lines.text: Ever stood at the open fridge, totally blank?
But here's the twist: the doorway made them forget more.
A doorway is an event boundary: new chapter, old one filed away.
lines.caps: A *DOORWAY IS | AN *EVENT BOUNDARY | NEW *CHAPTER | OLD ONE *FILED AWAY

lines.text: Going back? Nope, the first room didn't help.
Next Body File: sitting all day, the 'silent killer.' Now get up... wait, why?
